Use paired per-user hit differences on identical users and candidate sets: Δ = ¼Σcategory mean(hit_variant − hit_baseline). Bootstrap 200 paired users within each category, retaining four-category weighting, for a descriptive 95% interval; report category deltas and discordant hit counts. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. An exact McNemar test can supplement each category’s comparison. These estimates describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed candidates and seed; they do not measure training-seed variability or correct adaptive tuning. User resampling is discussed in this [recommender evaluation review](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-020-09371-3).

Predeclare checkpoint evaluation frequency, maximum epochs, patience and tie-breaking; apply identical rules to baseline, gate-only, loss-only and combined SASRec. Select using the prescribed macro validation HR@10, retain category results, and log every attempted configuration and inspected checkpoint. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training/evaluation seed 42, splits and evaluator unchanged. Repeated validation maximization creates selection optimism: ordinary bootstrap intervals around the selected winner cannot establish an unbiased improvement. Treat small gains as exploratory, apply Holm correction to three prespecified baseline comparisons if testing, and freeze the final choice before held-out evaluation. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) explain this selection bias.

Proposed budget: 3,600 GPU-seconds for baseline profiling and diagnostics; 28,800 for the four controlled comparisons, initially 7,200 each; 7,200 for one prespecified refinement; 3,600 reserved for failures and final artifact verification. Each comparison retains all four datasets. Reuse profiling work where valid and adjust allocations using measured throughput; completing 200 epochs cannot be guaranteed beforehand. Four concurrent slots reduce elapsed time, not aggregate GPU cost. Charge all training/debugging to 43,200 seconds; inspect no test labels.
